about: SSO attacks that play a faulty recording: one round robin with its own narrow tone. gen_spitfire_sso.py writes 'avoid' into the map (<Articulation avoid="keys:low-high:velocity">): an attack in the band plays at 'velocity', the nearest velocity measured clean. Measured 2026-10-10 with kthost and Kontakt 8 + SSO on the Windows test VM, the patches' MuseScore setups: 12 isolated attacks per render (0.5 s on, 0.4 s apart), CC1 64, CC11 102 (Whence's Celli under [levels] context); each render starts Kontakt afresh and renders identically (3 in a row per C3 velocity). Metric: per attack the peak in a band round the tone (band_hz; 50-350 ms after the note-on, 16384-point FFT) against the render's median attack: round_robin_5_db the faulty round robin's, largest_attack_db the largest of the 12 where none stands out. The owner heard it in Whence 1-16 strings (A, [levels] context): bars 1.3, 3.2, 5.1, 5.4, Celli C3 re-attacks at 106.

48.faulty: round robin 5 of 6 (attacks 5 and 11 of 12), peak 1184 Hz
48.note: 117-127 is the accented attack (another technique; Auto: under an accent or marcato): +6 dB, not avoided

47.faulty: the same recording a semitone down (1117 Hz)

Violas - Performance.note: Eb3 (51) at 90 and 106, F#3 (54) and A3 (57) at 106, one render each: the narrow-tone screen (each attack's spectrum over the 12's median, 300-4000 Hz) shows no round robin apart from the others (6-14 dB, as on the clean Celli renders); no band measured
